video.title: 3 businesses we think are about to blow up

summary: Sam Parr and Shaan Puri of My First Million pitch businesses they think will grow. The first is oxytocin nasal sprays marketed to save marriages, inspired by Palmer Luckey's answer and biohacking subreddits. The second is affinity or fraternal memberships such as the Knights of Columbus, Good Sam, USCCA and AARP, which monetise loneliness and identity through insurance and financial products. They also discuss Angel Studios' member-voted, values-based streaming ($450M ARR), A24's model of buying overlooked films and guerrilla marketing, and the poor economics of film. The takeaway is to spot fringe trends early and monetise trusted communities with commodity financial products.

speakers.name: Palmer Luckey
speakers.description: Founder of Anduril and Oculus, in a conference clip

ideas.name: Oxytocin nasal spray for couples/marriage bonding
ideas.one_liner: Package oxytocin (largely unregulated in the US, sold as powder) as a nasal spray positioned to 'end the tragedy of divorce' and help bonding, autism and social connection.
ideas.business_model: DTC product sales (telehealth-style brands like Hims/BlueChew may adopt it)
ideas.customer: Couples drifting apart; people with autism/Asperger's or PTSD seeking social connection; teams
ideas.problem: Divorce affects ~50% of people; social bonding difficulty
ideas.offer: Oxytocin nasal spray marketed for pair bonding

acquisition_channels.details: Hosts predict Meta ads claiming it will cure divorce within 12 months.
Positioning lifted from Palmer Luckey's viral answer.

ideas.delivery: Bulk oxytocin bought from chemical suppliers and formulated as a nasal spray; telehealth brands may sell it.

acquisition.how: Paid social and content ads automate, but health claims face ad-platform restrictions.

uk_applicability.notes: In the UK oxytocin is a prescription-only medicine (MHRA); selling it as a consumer product would be illegal. Advertising medical claims is also restricted.

risks: Ad platform bans on health claims

quotes.text: I would try to end the tragedy of divorce with oxytocin doping for marriage counseling
quotes.speaker: Palmer Luckey (clip)

quotes.text: I would not be surprised if in 12 months you and me and our listener are gonna get a lot of meta ads saying this will cure divorce
quotes.speaker: Sam Parr

ideas.name: Affinity/fraternal membership monetised with financial products
ideas.one_liner: Build an identity-based community (religious, RV owners, gun owners, retirees) with cheap dues and perks, and earn the real money selling or licensing insurance and financial products to members.
ideas.business_model: Membership dues plus insurance/financial products sold or white-labelled to members
ideas.customer: Members of a shared-interest community (e.g. Catholic men, RV owners, concealed-carry holders, over-50s)
ideas.problem: Loneliness; members want belonging, discounts and tailored insurance
ideas.offer: Membership with events, chapters, magazine, discounts and preferred insurance products

pricing.notes: Insurance is often provided by a partner (AARP licenses its name to UnitedHealthcare).

acquisition_channels.details: Local chapters at churches (14,000 chapters); AARP mails everyone turning 50/60.
AARP sends a letter to people above 50 or 60.

ideas.delivery: Volunteer chapters run events and charity drives; insurance partner underwrites.
unit_economics_claims: Knights of Columbus: 2-3M members, $30B assets, $5-10B annual revenue

acquisition.how: Community content and digital ads automate; chapter building is human.

delivery.how: Events and community need humans; insurance via partner.

uk_applicability.notes: Affinity membership works in the UK (e.g. Caravan and Motorhome Club, Saga), but selling insurance requires FCA authorisation or acting as an introducer/appointed representative.

risks: Healthcare shares may not be legally obligated to pay

quotes.text: the way they make money is they sell life insurance to their members and they crush it
quotes.speaker: Sam Parr

quotes.text: there's a lot of interesting opportunities to jump on this whole loneliness thing and monetize it via financial products
quotes.speaker: Sam Parr

ideas.name: Healthcare share programme
ideas.one_liner: Community members pool monthly payments instead of insurance premiums to cover each other's medical bills.

pricing.notes: Not legally obligated to pay claims.

uk_applicability.notes: US-specific: the UK has the NHS; a pooled health-cost scheme would be regulated insurance.

quotes.text: if anybody in the community has that $40,000 surgical bill, the group coordinates to get the money paid out
quotes.speaker: Shaan Puri

ideas.name: Values-based streaming studio (Angel Studios)
ideas.one_liner: Clean, values-based films and TV for a paying membership that votes on what gets greenlit.
ideas.customer: Families wanting content with no cursing, drugs or sex, and heroic stories
ideas.problem: Mainstream content is unsafe for kids
ideas.offer: Original and acquired clean movies/series (e.g. The Chosen); members vote; >70% approval needed

acquisition_channels.details: Viral marketing heritage of founder (Poo-Pourri, Squatty Potty).

ideas.delivery: Produces/acquires films; began as a filter removing content from Hollywood films (sued, ~$10M).

uk_applicability.notes: Values-based streaming could serve UK audiences; the US faith market is far larger.

quotes.text: if 70% of less than 70% green light it, the deal's dead no matter what
quotes.speaker: Sam Parr

quotes.text: 450 million in ARR, it's a public company
quotes.speaker: Sam Parr

ideas.name: A24-style indie studio picking up overlooked films
ideas.one_liner: Acquire low-budget, distinctive films the risk-averse studios ignore and market them with guerrilla stunts.
ideas.offer: Edgy differentiated films with brand, merch and stunt marketing

acquisition_channels.details: Guerrilla stunts: fake leaked Zoom trailer, in-character Instagram account, Super Bowl empty-seats stunt with paid influencers nearby.

ideas.delivery: Independent directors make films; studio markets.
unit_economics_claims: Example film: $14M to make, $40M marketing, $250M box office, ~50% kept

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK film market, which is smaller.

risks: Hits-driven: one hit must cover about six flops
Marketing often costs more than the film

quotes.text: That created an opportunity for folks like A24 who could go pick up at pretty low cost and pretty uncompetatively all the other films that were being ignored
quotes.speaker: Shaan Puri

ideas.name: Trusted IVF brand ('Chick-fil-A of IVF')
ideas.one_liner: Build a consumer brand people trust for fertility/IVF.
ideas.problem: Lack of a trusted brand in IVF

uk_applicability.notes: UK IVF is regulated by the HFEA; private clinics exist.

quotes.text: The idea there is to build a trusted brand in the IVF world to chain the Chick-fil-A of IVF
quotes.speaker: Sam Parr

ideas.name: 'Reaction to the action' counter-trend products
ideas.one_liner: Find the reaction to a dominant trend (Snapchat vs Facebook, GLP-1 vs abundant food, screen-time limiting devices like Brick).
ideas.customer: Consumers reacting to a mainstream trend

uk_applicability.notes: A general idea-generation method; works anywhere.

quotes.text: a great way to think of a business idea is to find the reaction to the action
quotes.speaker: Shaan Puri

tactics.name: Package a fringe trend with a killer one-line positioning
steps: Watch niche subreddits (biohacking) for early signals
Frame the product against a huge emotional problem (divorce)

quote.text: I follow these weird subreddits with biohacking. And this is how I learned about GLP1s
quote.speaker: Sam Parr

tactics.name: Affinity membership monetisation
steps: Charge modest dues with discounts that justify membership
Partner with an insurer and license your brand (AARP/United model)
Monetise via financial products members trust you for

tactics.name: Guerrilla stunt marketing
steps: Create an in-character social account without explaining
Stage an unexplained public stunt (empty Super Bowl seats, tuxedo, flowers)
Seat paid influencers nearby who will post about it

lessons.lesson: Fringe health trends often go mainstream (GLP-1s, peptides, psychedelics); niche forums show early signals.
Positioning can make a strange product compelling: tie it to a huge, emotional problem.
Community memberships can monetise through trusted financial products far more than through dues.
Loneliness is driving young men (30-40) into fraternal organisations.

quote.text: young men like between 30 and 40 are joining and it's their fastest growing segment
quote.speaker: Sam Parr

lessons.lesson: Look for the reaction to the dominant action as a source of ideas.
Big incumbents become risk-averse, leaving ignored inventory a challenger can buy cheaply.
In movies and games, marketing spend often exceeds production cost.
Strong values-based communities can greenlight and market products themselves.

evidence_quality.rationale: Second-hand speculation and recollected figures; Whisper transcript mis-hears names (Andrule, perivol). No first-hand operation.
